title: Adaptive edge chooser with quantile mix and link-quality escrow
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Design and implement a routing policy (edge chooser) that combines latency quantiles (p50/p95) and link-quality signals (packet loss, rtt variance, and egress errors) into a single decision score per POP. The policy must: 1) use short and long horizons (e.g., 1m/10m EWMA) to detect transient spikes vs sustained degradation; 2) apply tier-aware penalties so higher-paid tenants prefer lower-latency POPs while best-effort traffic can accept fallbacks; 3) provide hysteresis to avoid flapping; 4) support configurable fallback model variants (e.g., reduced-context or quantized variants) when regional capacity is constrained; 5) include safety escrow logic that prevents routing oscillation during rapid network churn by pinning active sessions to the last-known-good POP until downstream KV cache warmup is safe; and 6) emit diagnostic labels for Console and alerts (chosen_pop, score_components, reason_code).
acceptance_criteria: Decision score computed per POP combining p50, p95, packet_loss_pct, and egress_error_rate and visible in telemetry
Routes pick the POP with highest score after applying tier penalties and hysteresis rules
When a chosen POP reports capacity limit or variant-mismatch, route falls back to specified model variant in config and logs reason_code
No route flaps observed in synthetic churn test (90s of induced packet loss across two POPs) with <3 switches/hour per session
Dashboard with per-tenant pop selection breakdown, score components, and SLOs available in Console-telemetry (runtime-1.20 release tab)
Unit and integration tests for score calculation, hysteresis logic, and variant fallback paths
tasks: Design scoring function: normalized quantile blend (0.6*p50 + 0.4*p95) with multiplicative network-health penalty
Add EWMA and sliding-window baseline for anomaly suppression
Implement tier-penalty layer and tenant override config
Build safety escrow: session pinning + KV cache warmup detection
Implement model-variant mapping and automatic fallback plumbing
Expose score_components and reason_code on request logs and Console
Write unit tests + integration tests against simulated POPs
Create dashboard, alerts, and runbook for oncall
